correctness.rationale: The ordinary uncoloured partition series satisfies B(q)=B(q^m)/(1−q). Write G_r(q)=sum_{n≥1} b_m(m^r n−1)q^n. The recurrence for B gives G₁=qB/(1−q) and extraction gives G_r=B A_r with A₁=q/(1−q) and A_{r+1}=U_m(A_r/(1−q)). For a_r(x) the polynomial coefficient sequence of A_r, a₂(x)=mx and a_{r+1}(x)=sum_{j=1}^{mx}a_r(j). The normalization h_r=2^{r−2}a_r/m^{r−1} has h₂=x and is iterated by T_m f=(2/m)sum_{j=1}^{mx}f(j). In the monomial basis the Faulhaber coefficient of x^t in T_m x^k is 2m^{t−1} binom(k,t−1)B_{k+1−t}/t with the B₁ sign convention for sums starting at 1. Since 2B_j is dyadically integral, its coefficient valuation is ≥(t−1)a−ν₂(t)≥0. The Bernoulli bound also follows from vanishing of odd B_j beyond B₁ and the Bernoulli recursion at even j, which divides by the odd j+1. As T_m x=x+mx², h_r≡x modulo 2^a coefficientwise. Substituting in G_r and removing the odd factor (m/2^a)^{r−1} mod 2 gives the stated convolution and integer divisibility at every r≥2. At n=1 the convolution is b_m(0)=1, so the exponent is attained, including for m=2 and for all even non-prime-power bases. No finite checker run is needed to justify the infinite claim. The originality failure is not a counterexample to this proof.
residual_risks: The modulus statement concerns precisely the ordinary uncoloured family at m^r n−1; it does not establish valuations when the convolution is even or treat coloured partitions.

evidence: Rødseth–Sellers Theorem 1 gives the known lower modulus D_R on this branch, as well as branches with other shifts. The proof's kernel information is stronger than that theorem statement.

Żmija's varying-base theorem yields dyadic exponent sum_{s=1}^{r−1} max(a−floor(log₂ s),0) here. It is no stronger than e_{m,r}, and is smaller for a≥2 and r≥5; that theorem alone is not normalized parity.
Churchhouse's known binary valuation criterion already gives ν₂(b₂(2^r n−1))=1: neither 2^r n−1 nor 2^r n−2 is a positive multiple of 4 when r≥2.

evidence: Use their Eq. (29): D_i divides H_i in integer series. Lemma 2 writes H_R=m^(R(R+1)/2) h_R−sum_{1≤i<R} β_R(i)H_i, where h_R=q/(1−q)^(R+1) in the prior notation and m^(R−i)/2 divides β_R(i). For R≥2 the first term vanishes mod 2D_R. Every term with i≤R−2 vanishes too: (m^(R−i)/2)D_i=2^(R−1−i)D_R.

For i=R−1 the same proof gives β_R(R−1) ≡ β_{R−1}(R−2)−α_R(R−1) (mod m^(R−1)), using β_{R−1}(R−1)=1. Equation (10) has α_R(R−1)=−(R−1)(m−1)m^(R−1)/2, divisible by m for even m and R≥3. The base is β₂(1)=binom(m,2)≡m/2 (mod m). Hence β_R(R−1)/(m/2) is odd for every R≥2.

It follows that H_R/D_R ≡ H_{R−1}/D_{R−1} (mod 2), with H₁/D₁=q/(1−q)^2. Multiplication by B_m in the unshifted factorization gives exactly sum_{j=1}^n j b_m(n−j) mod 2. At n=1 it is one, so the same calculation proves sharpness.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: No new hypothesis or sharp estimate is needed: Lemma 2's off-diagonal bounds eliminate all but one term, and its published recurrence fixes that term modulo 2. This is demonstrable prior implication of the complete Finding, even though Theorem 1 does not explicitly print the normalized convolution.

originality.rationale: The full normalized parity claim, not just the universal divisor, is a direct consequence of Rødseth–Sellers' published kernel identities and coefficient bounds (2001). Passing to one bit above their published divisibility bound leaves only the adjacent-kernel term in Lemma 2, whose coefficient after normalization is odd by the recurrence in its proof and Eq. (10). This yields the entire claimed convolution for all even m, all r≥2 and all multipliers n, including the all-ones exact valuation. The alternative Bernoulli-operator proof is valid, but its theorem as stated in the Finding is already covered by that prior machinery.
residual_risks: Bibliographic priority is not claimed exhaustively; the demonstrated implication from one accessible prior paper suffices for coverage. The exact parity corollary need not have been separately printed there.

value.rationale: The index progression and the sharpness question are well motivated. But the exact invariant offered as the contribution is a routine one-bit refinement of the existing published triangular recurrence, with no distinct valuation case left outside that implication. The Bernoulli proof is an alternative explanation of the same Finding; the record does not establish an independently needed new theorem or a new use of the method beyond its parity and sharpness claim. No narrower surviving claim from this Finding is supplied as a repair.
residual_risks: This judgement is for the actual frozen claim, not for possible future generalizations of the dyadic operator.
